title: How does Norfolk's Zoning Ordinance decide what's allowed where, and how does a Conditional Use Permit work?
summary: General rules from the City's official Zoning Ordinance: how to read a use table (P, C, P/C, blank; unlisted uses are prohibited; an overlay district's column can allow or prohibit a use whatever the base district says), the standards a Conditional Use Permit is judged by and keeps being held to, when an approved permit lapses or can be revoked, how a conditional rezoning binds land only by the conditions City Council accepts, when a nonconforming use is abandoned, the Conditional Use Permit route for a Norfolk Historic Landmark outside the HC and HO districts, what the Official Zoning Map decides, and how to get a written interpretation. Which district an address is in comes from the City's open-data map layers (parcel_inventory), which Siren treats as a guide, not a legal determination; whether a particular use is allowed there needs that use's row, read in the district's column (and any overlay's column), from the ordinance itself (the zoning_uses tool reads the use tables). Who hears and decides a Conditional Use Permit (a Planning Commission hearing, then City Council) is in the norfolk-zoning-restaurant-ghent case file.

findings.claim: The ordinance's use tables say in which zoning districts each use is allowed and what kind of permit or review it needs (§3.1.4).

what_would_help.text: To see whether a use is allowed at an address, find its district first, then read the use's row in that district's column of the use table, and any overlay district's column: P allowed, C needs a Conditional Use Permit, P/C may need one depending on the use's performance standards; blank or unlisted means it can't be newly established there unless an overlay column allows it. Whether a proposed use fits a listed one is the Zoning Administrator's interpretation (§2.4.17), and an existing nonconforming use may be allowed to continue (§6.2.1).

For a binding answer about one property, a landowner, resident or business owner can ask the Zoning Administrator for a written interpretation (§2.3.8); if it isn't appealed in time, it becomes final.

If a Conditional Use Permit is approved, and unless the permit sets other terms, start construction or the use within 12 months, or ask the Zoning Administrator before it expires for an extension (up to six months, for good cause, if the use complies with the ordinance); a longer one needs City Council.

records_to_request: Written interpretations of the Zoning Ordinance issued by the Zoning Administrator under §2.3.8 in the last two years (Department of City Planning).
The list of Conditional Use Permits approved, denied and withdrawn by City Council in the last two years, with ordinance numbers (City Clerk).
pending: The use tables' individual rows are not findings here (a cell in a table column can't be quoted exactly from the PDF's text); the zoning_uses tool reads them from the same PDF, and ordinance_lookup reads the sections.

The Official Zoning Map is the final authority (§1.6.1), and the City's open-data Zoning layer that parcel_inventory reads is not it; whether and how often the layer is reconciled with the official map isn't stated in the ordinance.
How often Council approves or denies Conditional Use Permits: that would need the Council's legislation records, counted, not the ordinance.
The vesting provisions of the Code of Virginia that an expiring Conditional Use Permit is subject to (§2.4.8) are state law, not yet a finding.

Which conditional zoning districts exist and what their proffers say: the Conditional Zoning Index (§2.4.4) is kept in City Planning's offices and isn't published as a dataset the agent reads; each conditional rezoning's ordinance is a Council legislative record.

The exceptions under which an abandoned nonconforming use may continue (§6.2.4: historic or architecturally significant properties with a Conditional Use Permit, among others), and enlarging a nonconforming use by up to 50% with a Conditional Use Permit (§6.2.3), are not yet findings.

Which buildings are designated Norfolk Historic Landmarks: designations are marked on the Official Zoning Map (§2.4.7); whether the open-data layers parcel_inventory reads carry them hasn't been checked here.
